statement: The module supports 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi using 802.11b/g/n, with 802.11n bit rate up to 150 Mbps.
The module supports Bluetooth LE 5, including Bluetooth mesh and data rates from 125 Kbps to 2 Mbps.
The module provides up to 36 GPIOs and multiple interfaces including SPI, UART, I2C, I2S, USB, ADC, PWM, and touch sensing.
Wi-Fi transmit peak current is listed as 355 mA for 802.11b at 1 Mbps and 20.5 dBm.

statement: ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 is approximately 18.0 x 25.5 x 3.1 mm.
ESP32-S3-WROOM-1U is approximately 18.0 x 19.2 x 3.2 mm.
Module placement should minimize interference from the baseboard on antenna performance.
The module is moisture sensitivity level 3 and should be soldered within 168 hours after unpacking under the specified factory conditions.
The specified ESD ratings are plus or minus 2000 V for HBM and plus or minus 500 V for CDM.
The recommended lead-free reflow process uses SAC305 solder with a peak temperature of 235 to 250 C and a peak time of 30 to 70 seconds.
Datasheet versions v1.0 and higher are official releases; major changes are communicated through Product Change Notifications.
Datasheet v1.8 dated 2026-03-02 updated pin assignment information, added an SD/MMC note, and updated low-power current data.
For a single-supply design, 3.3 V is recommended and the supply output current should be no less than 500 mA.
An ESD protection diode and at least a 10 uF capacitor are suggested at the main power entrance.
VDD_SPI can operate at 1.8 V or 3.3 V, and additional 0.1 uF and 1 uF decoupling capacitors are recommended near VDD_SPI.
Power rails should stabilize for at least 50 microseconds before CHIP_PU is pulled high, and CHIP_PU should stay low for at least 50 microseconds during reset.
A typical reset RC network uses 10 kohm and 1 uF, but the values should be adjusted for the actual power supply.
A four-layer PCB is recommended; a two-layer design is also possible if it maintains an adequate ground plane.
The recommended main power-trace width is at least 25 mil, VDD3P3 traces at least 20 mil, and other power traces about 10 mil.
The RF trace should have approximately 50 ohm characteristic impedance and should be kept short with a complete adjacent ground reference.
High-frequency signal traces and interference sources such as crystals, USB, and UART should be kept away from the antenna and RF trace.
Octal SPI traces should have matching lengths, with suitable grounding and decoupling around flash and PSRAM.
A clearance of at least 15 mm in all directions is recommended around a PCB antenna inside the final product housing.
The final product should be tested for wireless throughput and communication range after the module is placed in its enclosure.
USB differential traces should target 90 ohm impedance with plus or minus 10 percent tolerance and equal-length routing.
Poor RF transmit or receive performance can result from crystal interference, nearby high-frequency traces, or RF impedance mismatch.
Firmware can be downloaded through UART or USB using the documented joint-download boot mode and GPIO0 configuration.
The guideline revision history identifies v1.8 dated 2025-07-03 and records updates to power, RF, UART, USB, touch, and schematic guidance.
